name: s3-protrusion-enclosure
title: Protrusions to enclosure — can protrusion mechanics reach stable wrapping?
question: Can an archaeal-like deformable host physically surround and enclose a bacterial partner from differential adhesion alone, and under which mechanical conditions does wrapping reach a stable topology rather than a partial cup or a transient contact?
hypothesis: The host engulfs the symbiont when host-symbiont adhesion beats the combined surface-tension cost (J_hs < J_sM - J_hM); stable enclosure is the emergent plateau of the host's coverage of the symbiont boundary, with a sharp transition in the mechanical parameters.
objective: Run the protrusion_enclosure CPM composite (campaign composite B) at strong vs weak host-symbiont adhesion, measure the enclosure fraction (host coverage of the symbiont boundary), and sweep the adhesion x symbiont-surface-tension plane to produce the enclosure phase diagram.
description: Gate G3 (Enclosure) of the viva-genesis eukaryogenesis campaign "The Endosymbiotic Transition", realized on the real Rust Cellular Potts engine (differential-adhesion engulfment, Glazier & Graner 1993 Fig. 18 physics). Replaces the analytical Helfrich-threshold stand-in with an emergent, measured spatial outcome.
claim: Differential adhesion alone drives a deformable host to stable enclosure of a symbiont in a well-defined mechanical regime (J_hs below the J_sM - J_hM threshold); below the transition the host forms only a partial cup or leaves the symbiont free.
expected_behavior: Under strong adhesion (low J_hs) the host coverage of the symbiont boundary rises to a stable plateau near 1.0 (full enclosure).
Under weak adhesion (high J_hs) coverage settles low (partial cup / free symbiont); the transition tracks J_hs = J_sM - J_hM.

readouts.name: Enclosure fraction
readouts.description: Host coverage of the symbiont boundary (symbiont faces touching host / all exposed symbiont faces); 1.0 = fully enclosed.

behavior_tests.name: Host reaches stable enclosure under strong adhesion
behavior_tests.description: With strong host-symbiont adhesion (J_hs=6, below the J_sM-J_hM=12 threshold) the host wraps the symbiont to a stable plateau. Measured from the composite run (40 steps x 60 MCS): enclosure_fraction=1.000.

behavior_tests.name: Weak adhesion leaves the symbiont free (failure route)
behavior_tests.description: With weak host-symbiont adhesion (J_hs=18, above threshold) the host cannot hold the symbiont; coverage settles low. Measured: enclosure_fraction=0.176.

Weak adhesion leaves the symbiont free (.notes: enclosure_fraction 0.176 at 2400 sweeps; free symbiont / partial cup

findings.statement: Differential adhesion alone drives stable enclosure in a well-defined mechanical regime: the adhesion x symbiont-surface-tension phase diagram shows a sharp transition tracking J_hs = J_sM - J_hM, with stable enclosure, partial wrapping, transient internalization, and no enclosure as distinct regimes.

conclusion: The CPM enclosure model reaches stable wrapping as an emergent outcome when adhesion beats the surface-tension cost, and the phase diagram maps where it can and cannot. This is the G3 enclosure plane of the endosymbiosis phase diagram and a candidate replacement for S3's analytical gate.
